commentary: The market environment is undergoing a sharp structural divergence between mega-cap technology/semiconductors and defensive/real-asset sectors. While tech growth names (QQQ, NVDA, GOOGL) have broken below their 200-day moving averages under valuation pressure, defensive sectors such as Healthcare (LLY) and Real Estate (VNQ), alongside Treasury bond hedges (TLT, IEF, AGG), are experiencing positive relative momentum. Market breadth of 58.6% reflects this split market rather than a full index breakdown. This book is positioned to trim failed momentum theses in growth assets, maintain our effective 31.5% Treasury hedge sleeve, and reallocate equity risk into non-tech momentum leadership and real assets while maintaining derived equal weighting across holdings. I would change my mind and increase bond exposure toward 40% if broad market breadth falls below 50% or if SPY breaks below its 200-day moving average.
allocation_reason: The target bond weight of 0.315 sits 6.5 percentage points above the 0.25 sleeve minimum and 43.5 percentage points below the 0.75 sleeve maximum. Treasuries have demonstrated strong inverse hedging performance over the past month (TLT +5.6%, IEF +3.0%) during equity volatility, confirming that maintaining a ~31.5% fixed income sleeve provides appropriate ballast while keeping 60.0% allocated to risk assets.
